chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a mother of the children of a man. So her master died, and for the deceased was a child from other than the mother of his children. What is your view if the one who married the mother of the children were to marry the daughter of her master who had emancipated her, so that he would gather between her and the daughter of her master who had emancipated her? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that.

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of the child (a concubine who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of the master who freed his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific nuance in the rules of *mahram* (prohibited kinship) by distinguishing between blood ties and ties created through emancipation (*umm al-walad*). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that marrying the daughter of the master who freed the wife is permissible, illustrating the Shia juristic principle that emancipation creates a distinct legal bond that does not necessarily preclude marriage with the master's other descendants, provided the specific prohibitions of direct lineage or nursing are not violated.
